title: A Trainable Spaced Repetition Model for Language Learning
venue: Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2016), Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 1848-1858
caption_short: What a Duolingo learner sees on a practice trial: the skill tree marking which skills are due for practice, a skill screen listing the learner's weakest words, and the graded translation exercise showing the correct-response and incorrect-response feedback screens.

notes: Cropped from a 220-dpi render of p. 2 of the ACL Anthology PDF. The four screenshot panels and their own (a)-(d) sub-labels are included; the 'Figure 1: Duolingo screenshots...' caption text below them is excluded. Chosen over Figure 4 (the forgetting-curve / half-life illustration, p. 5) because the task brief's primary criterion is what a participant sees and does, and Figure 1 is the only figure in the paper showing the actual practice interface and response feedback. Figure 4 on p. 5 is the alternative if a half-life / forgetting-curve illustration is wanted instead; Figure 3 on p. 3 shows the Leitner flashcard system.
